**Beaumont-Hamel British Cemetery** is a **Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC)** cemetery in **France**, on the former **Somme battlefield** near the village of **Beaumont-Hamel** in the department of **Somme, Hauts-de-France**.

## What it is
- A **First World War cemetery** containing the graves of British and Commonwealth soldiers.
- It is part of the wider battlefield landscape associated with the **Battle of the Somme** and, especially, the **Battle of the Ancre** in late 1916.
- It lies very close to the famous **Beaumont-Hamel Newfoundland Memorial Park** and the **Newfoundland Memorial** site, which commemorates the Royal Newfoundland Regiment’s action on **1 July 1916**.

## Historical background
- The cemetery was created during/after the fighting on the Somme, when graves were gathered from the battlefield and from smaller burial places in the area.
- The sector around Beaumont-Hamel saw extremely heavy fighting, particularly during the opening day of the Somme on **1 July 1916**, when the **Newfoundland Regiment** suffered devastating losses.
- The cemetery includes soldiers who died in the nearby attacks, as well as others from later actions in the same area.

## Who is buried there
- It contains **Commonwealth war burials from the First World War**.
- Most are British, but as with many CWGC cemeteries, there may also be men from other parts of the British Empire/Commonwealth.
- A number of the burials are **unknown soldiers**, which is common in Somme cemeteries because of the intensity of the fighting and the poor condition of remains after bombardment.
- Some graves may also be **reburials** from battlefield graves or smaller cemeteries nearby.

## Appearance and layout
- Like most CWGC cemeteries, it has:
  - a formal, carefully maintained layout,
  - standard **CWGC headstones**,
  - a **Cross of Sacrifice** and/or other CWGC features depending on the cemetery’s size and design.
- It is generally modest in size compared with the enormous battlefield cemeteries elsewhere on the Somme, but it is historically significant because of its location.

## Why it matters
Beaumont-Hamel British Cemetery matters because it stands in one of the most symbolically important parts of the Somme battlefield:
- it is tied to the **Newfoundland Regiment’s memorial landscape**,
- it marks the human cost of trench warfare,
- and it preserves the burial place of men who died in the fighting around **Beaumont-Hamel**.

## Visiting
- It is in a rural battlefield area and is typically visited together with the **Newfoundland Memorial Park** and other nearby Somme sites.
- The CWGC normally keeps it open and maintained as a place of remembrance.
